cases.age: UNVERIFIED (described only as a middle-aged man)
cases.exposure_context_quote: He was found at home foaming at the mouth lying next to a 100-mL bottle of insecticide, along with alcohol.
cases.agent: malathion (maldison) — Horti-on insecticide, 500 g/L maldison with 487 g/L liquid hydrocarbon solvent
cases.agent_quote: The paramedics had brought along the bottle of the ingested agent (Horti-on insecticide – 500 g/L maldison, an anticholinesterase compound, and solvent 487 g/L liquid hydrocarbon).
cases.route: ingestion (OP ingestion; found at home, conveyed by ambulance)
cases.circumstance: Found at home foaming at the mouth next to a 100-mL bottle of insecticide, along with alcohol; circumstances (intent) not explicitly stated.

symptoms.finding: foaming at the mouth; drowsy and diaphoretic
symptoms.quote: Paramedics found him drowsy and diaphoretic, and he was conveyed via ambulance to the nearest hospital.

symptoms.finding: unconscious with pinpoint pupils, clothing soaked in vomitus
symptoms.quote: He was unconscious and diaphoretic with pinpoint pupils, and his clothing was soaked in vomitus.
The patient had a heart rate of 152 bpm, blood pressure of 149/100 mmHg, respiratory rate of 20 bpm and an oxygen saturation of 100% on non-rebreather mask.

cases.time_to_care: found at home and conveyed via ambulance (exact interval UNVERIFIED)

labs.name: serum cholinesterase (day of ingestion)
labs.quote: Serum cholinesterase level taken on the day of ingestion was < 1000 U/mL and remained low until Day 5, when it increased to 1169 U/mL.

labs.name: serum cholinesterase (Day 5)
labs.quote: remained low until Day 5, when it increased to 1169 U/mL

labs.name: RBC cholinesterase
labs.quote: Red blood cell (RBC) cholinesterase was 3221 U/mL [Figure 1].

treatment.name: emergency intubation; HAZMAT decontamination (clothing removed, skin washed with liquid soap and running water)
treatment.quote: A decision was made for emergency intubation to promptly secure his airway. Thereafter, the hazardous material (HAZMAT) decontamination unit (HDU) located outdoors and adjacent to the resuscitation zone was activated.

treatment.name: pralidoxime (two 1-g doses over 30 min) and atropine (2.4 mg followed by 4.8 mg infusion)
treatment.quote: treatment with pralidoxime (two 1-g doses over 30 min) and atropine (2.4 mg followed by 4.8 mg infusion) was initiated for the patient.

treatment.name: propofol and fentanyl infusions; ICU admission; further pralidoxime and atropine; extubation Day 4
treatment.quote: Propofol and fentanyl infusions were used for post-intubation sedation and analgesia, and the patient was admitted to the intensive care unit for further management. ... He was extubated successfully on Day 4 after further treatment with pralidoxime and atropine and was moved to the high dependency unit for the next 3 days.

cases.icu_admission: yes (admitted to the intensive care unit; high dependency unit for 3 days after extubation)
cases.outcome: survived; discharged in full recovery (extubated Day 4, HDU 3 days, one more day in general ward)
cases.outcome_quote: He recovered uneventfully in the general ward for one more day before discharge in full recovery.
cases.notes: The paper is an incident analysis of secondary exposure among 14 healthcare workers who developed non-specific symptoms after contact with this patient; none showed typical OP toxidrome or significant cholinesterase reduction, so HCWs are not extracted as pesticide-poisoning cases.
